definitions.gloss: the five elements (wood, fire, earth, metal, water)
definitions.explanation: The five fundamental elements of traditional Chinese natural philosophy, thought to generate and overcome one another in cycles. Widely used in East Asian thought.

examples.japanese: {五行|ごぎょう}は{木|もく}・{火|か}・{土|ど}・{金|ごん}・{水|すい}から{成|な}る。
examples.english: The five elements consist of wood, fire, earth, metal, and water.

examples.japanese: {陰陽|おんよう}{五行|ごぎょう}の{考|かんが}え{方|かた}は{今|いま}も{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: The yin-yang and five-elements way of thinking still survives today.

examples.japanese: {東洋|とうよう}{医学|いがく}や{占|うらな}いは、{五行|ごぎょう}の{思想|しそう}に{深|ふか}く{影響|えいきょう}を{受|う}けている。
examples.english: Eastern medicine and fortune-telling are deeply influenced by the philosophy of the five elements.

notes:
The five elements of traditional Chinese natural philosophy — {木|もく} (wood), {火|か} (fire), {土|ど} (earth), {金|ごん} (metal), and {水|すい} (water). The elements are thought to generate and overcome one another in cycles.

RELATED WORDS:
- {陰陽|おんよう}{五行|ごぎょう}: the yin-yang and five-elements cosmology
- {五行説|ごぎょうせつ}: the theory of the five elements

USAGE:
The concept underlies much of traditional East Asian medicine, fortune-telling, and the calendar.
